channel.title: NextGen Chartered Accountant: UK tax and accounting updates
channel.description: New UK tax, payroll and Companies House rules, explained for small businesses, landlords and individuals.

item.title: Employer PAYE bill looks wrong? What to check before disputing it with HMRC
item.description: Compare your payroll submissions, HMRC account and payment records to find the difference. If the figures still do not agree, here is what to send HMRC.

item.title: Paying staff early for Christmas 2026? Which date to report to HMRC
item.description: If you bring forward regular December wages for Christmas, keep the normal payday on your Full Payment Submission. Here is how to check the dates before you run payroll.

item.title: Business Asset Disposal Relief lifetime limit halves to £500,000 from 6 April 2027
item.description: From 6 April 2027 the lifetime limit for Business Asset Disposal Relief falls from £1 million to £500,000. Here is who is affected, how past claims count and the rules for contracts signed before the change.

item.title: Capital allowances: 50% first-year allowance from January 2027, main rate writing-down allowance cut to 12%
item.description: The main rate first-year allowance rises from 40% to 50% for spending from 1 January 2027, while the main rate writing-down allowance falls from 14% to 12% from April 2027. What it means for sole traders and companies buying equipment.

item.title: Over 100,000 companies a year file their Company Tax Return more than 12 months late: what directors should know
item.description: HMRC says more than 100,000 companies a year file their Company Tax Return over a year late. Returns are due even when there is no tax to pay, and directors stay legally responsible.

item.title: Company cars and medical cover move into payroll from 6 April 2027: what employers need to do
item.description: From 6 April 2027 company cars, car fuel, vans, van fuel and medical benefits leave employees' tax codes and must be reported and taxed through payroll in real time, with Class 1A NICs paid through payroll too.

item.title: Moved to Making Tax Digital in April 2026? Your 31 January 2027 payments may show in two accounts
item.description: HMRC is writing to people who joined Making Tax Digital for Income Tax from 6 April 2026. The amounts due on 31 January 2027 may be split between your Self Assessment statement and your MTD account.

item.title: Payroll bureaus must register with HMRC as tax advisers by 17 February 2027
item.description: Phase three of HMRC's tax adviser registration is open. Professionals who only provide payroll services for clients and do not have an agent services account must register by midnight on 17 February 2027.

item.title: Landlords and savers: new 24%, 44% and 49% income tax rates from 6 April 2027
item.description: Budget 2026 introduced separate income tax rates for property and savings income. From 6 April 2027 they will be 24% basic, 44% higher and 49% additional rate.

item.title: Trading allowance to rise from £1,000 to £3,000 from April 2027
item.description: Budget 2026 confirmed the trading allowance will triple to £3,000 from the 2027 to 2028 tax year, with the Self Assessment reporting threshold for this income rising to £3,000 too.

item.title: Companies House identity verification one year on: what to do if a director has still not verified
item.description: The 12-month transition for existing directors ended on 17 November 2026. Companies House says enforcement is under way, with warning letters, prosecutions and planned notes on the public register.

item.title: Self Assessment scams: how to spot a fake HMRC message before 31 January
item.description: HMRC has had 1,704 reports of Self Assessment scams in the last 12 months. Here is how the fake refund scams work and what HMRC will never do.

item.title: Payroll deadlines every month: FPS on or before payday, pay HMRC by the 22nd
item.description: Running payroll means two HMRC deadlines every tax month. Here is the calendar, from payday to the 22nd, and what happens if you miss it.

item.title: VAT return deadline: one month and 7 days after each quarter, and the penalty points system
item.description: Your VAT return and payment are due by the same date. How the deadline works, why weekends do not count, and how late returns earn penalty points.

item.title: Company accounts: due 9 months after your year end, and the late filing penalties
item.description: Companies House expects your accounts 9 months after the financial year ends (21 months for first accounts). Penalties start at £150 and double if you are late two years running.

item.title: Corporation tax: pay 9 months and 1 day after your year end, file the CT600 within 12 months
item.description: The tax is due before the return. The two corporation tax deadlines, the late filing penalties, and what happens after 6 months.

item.title: Start your 2025 to 2026 tax return now: five things to check before 31 January
item.description: Around 5 million people leave their tax return until January. Here are the points worth checking now, including the Winter Fuel Payment, Child Benefit and crypto gains.

item.title: HMRC late payment interest rises to 8% from 24 November 2026
item.description: The Bank of England raised base rate to 4.00%, so HMRC's interest on late tax goes up to 8% a year. Here is what it means for anyone with a tax bill due on 31 January.

item.title: Making Tax Digital for Income Tax: five myths, and the next deadline on 7 February
item.description: Quarterly updates are not tax returns and no tax is paid with them. What sole traders and landlords in MTD need to know before the third update.

item.title: National Living Wage rises to £13.21 from April 2027: what employers should do now
item.description: The minimum wage goes up for every age group on 1 April 2027. Here are the new rates and the payroll checks worth doing before then.

item.title: Companies House: all accounts must be filed through software from April 2028
item.description: Small companies will not have to file a profit and loss account after all, but web and paper filing of accounts will close in April 2028.

item.title: Objecting to a company being struck off: online only from 1 December 2026
item.description: If a customer's company owes you money and is about to be struck off, Companies House will stop accepting objections by email from 1 December 2026. Here is how the online service works and what evidence you need.

item.title: Companies House identity verification: what directors and PSCs must do
item.description: Directors and people with significant control must verify their identity. Without it, a company cannot file its confirmation statement.

item.title: Dividend tax rates for 2026 to 2027: what company directors now pay
item.description: The basic and higher dividend rates went up by 2 percentage points from 6 April 2026. What it means for directors who take salary and dividends.

item.title: Capital gains tax in 2026 to 2027: rates, the £3,000 allowance and the new 18% BADR rate
item.description: Most gains are taxed at 18% or 24%, the annual exempt amount stays at £3,000, and Business Asset Disposal Relief now gives 18%.

item.title: The £90,000 VAT threshold: when you must register and how the 12-month test works
item.description: Registration is based on a rolling 12 months, not your tax year. How to check, the 30-day rules, and what happens if you register late.
